title: Shared ring buffer for ingest normalizer + ASCII-bypass zero-copy path
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: The prefill-side prompt ingest pipeline performs multiple allocation+copy stages for common prompt shapes (short ASCII prompts, repeated prefixes, session metadata). These copies increase CPU time before the model kernels run and push some requests into slower kernel selection paths because the sequence-length distribution is noisier.

Proposal: Implement a shared ring buffer and a two-tier normalization pipeline that: (1) routes ASCII-only prompts into a zero-copy fast-path that writes directly into the ring buffer with in-place normalization (lowercasing/whitespace collapse) and pointerized tokenization hints, (2) uses a compact shared buffer pool for multi-segment prompts to avoid per-request mallocs, and (3) emits metadata to the kernel selection layer so small predictable sequences are scheduled on low-latency kernels rather than general-purpose decode lanes.

Goals: reduce prefill CPU per-request by 30-45% for small prompts (<=256 bytes) on p3/p4 instances, reduce tail latency variance caused by allocation jitter, and reduce the number of requests that fall back to the higher-latency decode scheduling path because of noisy prefill timing.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change tokenizer semantics or implement new tokenization algorithms; it focuses on buffer management, normalization fast-paths, and scheduling hints for the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: ASCII-only prompts (single segment <=256 bytes) use the zero-copy path and show >=30% CPU reduction in the prefill stage compared to baseline
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for small chat prompts improves by >=10% under 95th percentile load
No semantic changes to tokenization outputs for any input (tests against canonical tokenizer suite pass)
Kernel-selection receives scheduling hints and metric hooks; rollout toggled by config flag runtime.ingest.fastpath.enabled
Memory usage of shared buffer pool under peak load stays within 15% of baseline (no unbounded growth)
work_items: Design shared ring buffer API and allocator semantics (lock-free where possible)
Implement ASCII-detection heuristic and in-place normalization routine (vectorized where safe)
Expose lightweight scheduling hint to runtime (sequence_class: SHORT_ASCII|REGULAR)
Add integration tests against tokenizer canonical suite and fuzz harness
Benchmark harness: microbench with varied prompt sizes and mixed workloads
Rollout plan: feature-flagged A/B on 10% of traffic, monitor latency and kernel path distribution
comments: 2026-02-18 - Liam Chen: Created ticket after spike showed ~28% CPU spent in pre-normalization copies on small prompts. Attached initial microbench results and heap flame. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ingest-shared-buffer-design

2026-02-24 - Priya Nair: Design review summary: we prefer a single-producer single-consumer lock-free ring for the hot path; fallback to small pooled slabs for multi-segment prompts. Edge case: very large system messages should skip the ring and use existing path.

2026-02-28 - Rafael Gomez (review): Reviewed vectorized normalization code; flagged UTF-8 boundary handling for multibyte sequences. Recommendation: ensure safe fallback to scalar path and add property-based tests for combining emojis with ZWJ sequences.

2026-03-03 - Priya Nair: Implemented prototype of ring buffer and ASCII-detect; local linux/p3 microbench shows 38% reduction in prefill CPU for 64B prompts, 22% for 128B. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/compare/eng-80123-ringbuffer

2026-03-06 - QE (Maya Singh): Integration tests failing intermittently in racey allocation path when under heavy concurrency. Added repro harness and stress test. Assigned follow-up to Rafael and Priya.
2026-03-10 - Priya Nair: Fixed race by adding per-shard freelist with ABA counter; reran stress tests for 1h, no repro. Updated PR with comments: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4128

2026-03-12 - Performance (Hiro Tanaka): End-to-end benchmark on p4x2 cluster: median latency down 12% under 50% small-prompt load; 95th down 11%. Kernel path telemetry shows 48% of short prompts now scheduled to short-latency kernel. Ready to begin canary rollout.
benchmarks: Baseline: prefill CPU 2.9ms/request median for 64B prompts (p3.2xlarge), prototype: 1.8ms/request median (-38%)
End-to-end: baseline 95th=120ms, prototype 95th=107ms under 50% small-prompt mix (-11%)
Memory: buffer pool steady-state +9% vs baseline under synthetic burst pattern (within goal)
blockers: Final sign-off needed from security on shared buffer allocator to ensure no information leakage between requests (KMS/tenant isolation review)
Monitoring: need new metric instrumentation for short-path usage and kernel-selection hint acceptance to make rollout safe
Conservative kernels: some legacy kernels don't accept scheduling hints; will need a compatibility shim or fallback mapping
